results.corrected_extracted: No long-term randomized studies of alcohol and ischaemic heart disease exist; short-term studies show dose-dependent effects on surrogate markers (higher HDL cholesterol, less platelet activation, lower fibrinogen, anti-inflammatory effects), and HDL cholesterol is also raised by regular heavy drinking and is highest in people with alcohol use disorder.
